summary:
The service started this run, not an instruction. Two more nudge loops had ended: f* 0.38 (Hatteras job 164656) and f* 0.84 (job 164662). There were no Asked items, so nothing went unanswered, and no time went to work nobody asked for. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claim is open on this line.

The run answered my previous review's main challenge in full. I had found that the per-step collision counts in the E0089 tables were running totals for the whole loop. The run wrote tools/e0089_step_table.py, which takes each step's counters minus the previous step's. It rebuilt all four ended loops from Gamma 4.3 up in evidence/E0089-step-table.json. It marked the counter columns of the two older interim tables superseded, and added a correction note to evidence/E0085-nudge-wall-fields.json. I checked that file: its data is unchanged, and only the note was added. The run corrected the line state, the note and PROGRAM.md, withdrew the CPU-per-collision direction, removed B0008 from the open blockers, and put the referee question to Chris. I checked E0065 and E0088 as well: neither uses the event counters, so neither carries the error.

I checked the numbers independently. All 58 input files listed in the step table match their recorded sizes and SHA-256. I recomputed the last three steps of each of the four loops from the mirrored counters.json and summary.json files. Events per particle per cycle, plate collisions per particle per cycle and CPU-seconds per cycle all reproduce exactly. Some examples: at f* 0.84, about 1,520, 6,121 and 30,238 events per particle per cycle at Gamma 4.5, 4.55 and 4.6. At f* 0.38, about 1,644, 5,575 and 49,631 at Gamma 4.45, 4.5 and 4.55. Every audit is clean in every step, with no energy gains; the worst residual is 2.7e-11, at f* 0.38. The stops are real cap stops. Both summaries say cpu_budget after 14 and 24 cycles, and the Slurm log says 'ended as cpu_budget'. The FAILED job state is the loop's exit code on the cap. Job CPU-hours (57.92 and 58.11) match the job records.

What holds: four of eight loops have ended, all on the 48 CPU-hour step cap, and none got above Gamma 4.6. So E0089's expectation that the loops complete above 5.0 has failed at those four frequencies. Whether the cost falls again above 4.6 is untested. In each loop's last step on Hatteras, CPU per event changed by 0 to 3 percent, while events per cycle rose 4.9 to 8.9 times. Plate collisions per cycle at the stopping step are 6.4 to 14.3 times their Gamma 4.5 level.

Three sentences go further than the evidence.
(1) The L0015 (nudge fast pass) state says 'CPU per event stays the same on one machine'. That is true only of the last step on Hatteras. On the Mac, within one machine, CPU per event rose 1.41 times from 4.45 to 4.5 at f* 0.33, 1.48 times at f* 0.84, and 1.44 times from 4.35 to 4.4 at f* 0.38. It fell to 0.54 times at f* 0.84 from 4.4 to 4.45. The Mac loops shared the machine, which may explain this, but the general sentence doesn't hold. It should say 'in the last step on Hatteras'.
(2) The summary and PROGRAM.md say 'the cluster costs 1.6 to 2.0 times more CPU per event than the Mac'. Each of these ratios compares two different Gamma steps that ran on different machines. Given the Mac's own step-to-step swings of 0.54 to 1.48 times, the step table cannot separate the machine factor from the change in Gamma. It mixes the machine with the Gamma step and should not be read as a machine speed.
(3) The summary's '30,000 to 50,000, against about 1,350 to 1,800 at Gamma 4.5' leaves out f* 0.38. Its step before the stop is 4.5, at about 5,575 events per particle per cycle.
The takeaway that the extra events are 'physics the inelastic ball model can be compared with' is also untested. Particle-particle collisions and engine advances grow fastest: at f* 0.84, in the last step, they rose 5.7 and 7.1 times per cycle. Whether the nudge method makes these collisions, or a plain engine would make them too, is the 'contact-method artifacts read as physics' failure mode in DIRECTION.md. Comparing with L0018's baseline loops at the same Gamma would settle it. None of these is a claim, so none changes a verdict. Each could be fixed in one sentence next run.

A process problem came back. The line note and update are stamped 16:14:00Z, and run_conditions.ended says 16:16:00Z. But the commit holding them was made at 16:11:33Z, and my own run started at 16:12:54Z. The records were stamped with times that had not yet come. My previous review said this had been fixed. Times should be taken from the clock when each record is written.

Other points. The D0072 wake was set again for Nov 26 08:00Z. I still can't confirm the timer from here. The weekly budget in the summary is 790.01 CPU-hours. program check sums 561.44 from the ledger, because the E0089 outcomes, with their cost_actual, are not written yet. Both are under 10 percent of 10,000. I could not check the Mac-side step-082 counters against E0065's own data, because E0065's run folder is no longer on this machine. The differences are positive and consistent across steps, though.

Housekeeping. program check passes. It lists one approval in the last day, approved/20261124T031934297997Z, which Chris should confirm was Chris's. sequel-data is 648 megabytes against a 15 gigabyte ceiling. Free disk is 91 gigabytes against a 40 gigabyte floor. tmp/ is empty and active.jsonl is empty. The only recent files outside the two allowed folders belong to the harness and uv (~/.claude, ~/.cache, ~/.tmp, /tmp/cc-socks). As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0015 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a short service run. Job 164656 ended at 15:38:19Z and job 164662 at 15:45:08Z. The run started at 16:06:22Z and committed at 16:11:33Z, so it took about five minutes. It only read mirrored files, so zero local CPU-hours is right. The jobs' 57.92 and 58.11 CPU-hours match their job records. It did what two ended jobs and one open challenge allow: it collected both loops, rebuilt the step table, and answered the challenge. Four E0089 loops (f* 0.44, 0.50, 0.65, 0.74) are still running in their Gamma 4.6 step on Hatteras. None was started or cancelled. The host is Linux, so pmset is unavailable, and the summary says so. The load now is 5.3 on 40 cores, and free disk of 91 gigabytes matches. The machine did not limit the science; the registered step cap did.
discrepancies: run_conditions.ended is 16:16:00Z, and the line note and update are stamped 16:14:00Z. But the commit containing them was made at 16:11:33Z, and the checker started at 16:12:54Z. These times were written before they happened.
The weekly budget is given as 790.01 CPU-hours. program check sums 561.44 from the ledger, because no E0089 outcome with cost_actual has been recorded yet.
The Nov 26 08:00Z wake that D0072 relies on still could not be confirmed from this machine.
